title: Credit Suisse HOLT Valuation 2019 -  Expedia vs Booking.com
description: Investment Pitch Spring 2019: EXPEDIA GROUP - USA EXPE Vs BOOKING HOLDINGS - USA BKNG. Created with the support of Holt Lens from Credit Suisse.

asr.full_text: Hello, I am Andrea Zaffino from Politecnico di Milano and today I am going to compare Expedia and Booking.com Online Travel services is a promising growth industry and Booking and Expedia are the winners of the consolidation process in such market Booking is the leader in International markets but Expedia has a larger presence in the US The two companies have two very different business models Booking adopts the agency model and acts as an intermediary between customers and travel service providers like hotels. Its revenue model is based on commissions just like the old brick and mortar travel agencies. On the contrary EXPEDIA adopts a merchant model, buying the service itself early on in bulk and reselling it to customers. The agency model has worked better in the past and is expected to continue doing so, thanks to lower costs and higher margins and this is reflected by the very different market capitalizations of the 2 competitors. Moreover, Expedia offers diversified services and even travel packages while booking focuses on hotels. Analyzing the historical data about the two companies, we can notice that Booking has had a higher sales growth and margin during the last years. Also, its lower asset turns show that Booking has been investing more than Expedia. Now, using the Hold Valuation method, we can see how this result impacts the two companies' returns. both of them have kept CFROI much higher than their cost of capital. In the last 4 years, Expedia has invested way beyond this normalized growth rate, and this is leading to increasing forecasted returns for the next 2 years. On the contrary, Booking has decreased spending in 2018, and we see a CFROI decrease in 2019. Anyway during the last last years both companies were granted stable returns to their shareholders, consistently doubling the S&P 500. Before giving our final investment recommendations, We need to consider some more critical factors. Despite similar price trends it is evident that booking has been consistently over valued. Moreover, both companies have lately been cautious on M&A's, focusing on organic growth, but future big acquisitions are not to be excluded. Both companies are a great investment opportunity at the moment, but despite the weaker momentum, I would recommend Booking.com, which is showing a better overall scorecard rank, higher prospective growth and more solid and sustainable business model.
